scenes.headline: How a 2005 Windows racer runs in a browser
scenes.sub: Most Wanted's own executable, translated to WebAssembly
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Wainscot! Need for Speed Most Wanted now runs in a browser tab, and nobody had its source code. So how?

scenes.text: It translates EA's own speed.exe to WebAssembly ahead of time, then rebuilds the parts of Windows the game calls.
scenes.say: The idea: translate the game's own executable to WebAssembly once, ahead of time, and rebuild the Windows it calls.

scenes.title: From one executable to a browser tab

steps.say: Start with the executable a player installs. A disassembler finds every function and jump target in it.
Each is translated once, at build time. The names are the disassembler's, never EA's.
Out comes one WebAssembly module. There is no just in time compiler.
The game still calls Windows, so a host answers: threads, exceptions, input, and Direct three D nine, drawn with WebGPU.

scenes.title: Where static translation breaks
scenes.say: Translating ahead of time has two classic failure points.

items.say: A jump to a computed address must land on a block the translator already knows.
And an instruction it does not model must never run.
Old mods patched bytes. Here, fixes replace whole functions by address.

scenes.title: Game files, eight megabytes at a time

steps.say: Only the executable is copied whole. Every other file stays on a third-party CDN.
When the game reads, the tab fetches eight megabyte blocks and keeps them.
The game just sees a folder under Program Files.

scenes.label: addresses inside speed.exe in the symbol table it ships
scenes.note: all named by Ghidra, none by EA

scenes.title: Two ways to port without asking

left.title: GTA V, from source
left.say: The GTA Five port compiled Rockstar's leaked source, names and all, and swapped its platform layer.

right.title: Most Wanted, from the binary
right.say: This one had only the executable. So it runs exactly the original code, and rebuilds Windows around it.

scenes.text: With no source, the original game logic is kept exactly, and the hard work moves to Windows, shaders and files.
scenes.say: With no source, the game's own logic survives exactly. The hard work moves to the edges: Windows, the shaders and the files.

recap: EA's speed.exe, translated ahead of time
Windows and Direct3D 9 rebuilt on WebGPU
Retail files streamed from a third-party CDN
scenes.say: The executable, translated once. Windows, rebuilt on WebGPU. And the game's files, streamed from someone else's server.
